adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, `createEvent` now takes an `externalId?: string` but does not pass it to the adapter; it only passes `credential.id` into `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and then echoes `externalId` back on the returned `EventResult` (`externalId, credentialId: credential.id`). In `packages/core/EventManager.ts#createAllCalendarEvents`, the loop calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination, so the recorded `result.externalId` is per-iteration, but the adapter’s actual calendar selection can differ because it re-selects from `event.destinationCalendar`.

This drift is verifiable in the diff: multiple adapters ignore `credentialId` entirely and just use the first destination calendar (e.g., Lark `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`, Office365 similarly, and `BaseCalendarService` filters by only the first destination’s `externalId`). In those cases, during the per-destination loop the event may be created on the first destination calendar, while the stored `externalId` in the result is `destination.externalId` for a different element—leading to references (`externalCalendarId` derived from `result.externalId`) pointing to a calendar the event wasn’t written to. Even in Google, `.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` can pick a different element than the current loop `destination` if multiple destinations share a credentialId or ordering differs.
